key_insight: Task-specific adaptation of an echocardiographic foundation model improved detection of PE-associated right-heart phenotypes compared with direct transfer.
clinical_relevance: AI-assisted bedside cardiac ultrasound could support recognition of PE-related right-heart strain, but these findings do not establish a standalone PE diagnostic tool.
method: Introduced HOPE: emergency cardiac ultrasound videos from 4,069 patients with suspected PE across five views.
Built EchoPE using EchoPrime-pretrained representations, view recognition, task-specific adaptation, and attention-based interpretability.
Low-Rank Adaptation plus knowledge distillation best balanced discrimination with preservation of pretrained echocardiographic semantics.
evidence_signal: With positive PE cases confirmed by CT pulmonary angiography, EchoPE achieved AUROC 95.2 ± 0.3% versus 87.6 ± 1% for EchoPrime with a classification head; precision at 90% sensitivity was 87.8% versus 70.7%.
watch_item: External validation and prospective clinical impact are not reported in the abstract, leaving generalizability and workflow utility uncertain.
paper_title: Adapting Echocardiographic Foundation Models for Detecting Pulmonary Embolism-Related Right-Heart Strain
